title: Code Node Mastery: JavaScript, Python, and External Libraries
summary: This day covers essential concepts for building AI engineering skills.
topics: n8n Code node (JavaScript and Python) and item structure
Using npm/Python packages in self-hosted n8n
Error handling and 'continue on fail' in code
When to use code vs built-in nodes (maintainability)
practical_task_reference: Write an n8n Code node (JavaScript) that correctly processes an array of items, uses an external library to transform data (e.g., a date or crypto library), preserves item pairing, and handles a failing item without stopping the batch.
mini_project_reference: Build a workflow with a Python (or JS) Code node that imports an external library to parse a non-trivial file format from binary input, transforms the data, outputs clean items, and uses continue-on-fail with failures routed to an error branch.
assignment_reference: Explain the n8n item structure and the run-once-per-item vs once-for-all-items modes, and give two examples of when using code is justified and two when a built-in node is the better choice.
